title: 2008 AMC 12B Problem 1
statement: A basketball player made \(5\) baskets during a game. Each basket was worth either \(2\) or \(3\) points. How many different numbers could represent the total points scored by the player?

solutions.text:
The total ranges from \(5 \cdot 2 = 10\) (all two-pointers) to \(5 \cdot 3 = 15\) (all three-pointers). Swapping one two-pointer for a three-pointer raises the total by exactly \(1,\) so every integer in between occurs.

The possible totals are \(10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15,\) which is \(6\) values.

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: The total is smallest with all \(2\)-point baskets and largest with all \(3\)-point baskets
Every integer between \(5 \cdot 2\) and \(5 \cdot 3\) is attainable
